title.narrative: NDI, Lokala samhällen med integritet (integrity driven communities)

description.narrative: Nordmakedoniens regering har uttryckt att bekämpning av korruption är en prioritet. Detta bekräftas av det fleråriga arbetsprogram som lades fram i oktober 2024. Det lyfts också fram inom ramen för EU-kommissionens tillväxtplan för Västra Balkan. Sverige stödjer arbetet mot korruption i Nordmakedonien genom olika program som bidrar till EU-närmande, grävande journalistik och förbättrad offentlig styrning på central nivå. Med det föreslagna stödet skulle Sverige även bidra till att stärka arbetet på kommunal nivå, där korruption ofta påverkar vanliga medborgare och i synnerhet redan utsatta grupper som etniska minoriteter, ungdomar och kvinnor. NDI är en internationell expertorganisation och etablerad partner till Sida. NDI bedöms ha kunskap om regionen samt god kapacitet och tillgång till global expertis. En utvärdering visar på tidigare framgångar i ett program om att stärka kvinnors politiska deltagande i Nordmakedonien. Sidas sammantagna bedömning är därför att samarbetet tidigare har fungerat väl med NDI och att de besitter en relativt unik lokal kompetens och förmåga att verka inom detta område i landet. Huvudmålet för programmet är att skapa starka system för att förebygga korruption i kommunerna och stärka medborgarnas förtroende för den offentliga förvaltningen. Detta ska göras genom: Att kommunerna får bättre verktyg för att identifiera och hantera korruption. Att civilsamhället och medierna stärks så att de kan övervaka och påverka beslut och tjänster på kommunal nivå. Programmet kommer också att stödja centrala myndigheter i att uppmuntra kommunerna att följa goda principer som transparens, ansvarsskyldighet och inkludering, särskilt inom områden med hög risk för korruption såsom offentlig upphandling och rekrytering. Digitalisering är en viktig del av projektet för att minska möjligheten till korruption. Kommunerna uppmuntras att öppna upp sina data och använda digitala system för att visa att de är transparenta och ansvariga. För att göra programmet mer effektivt och få större genomslag avses samfinansiering med Schweiz, en givare har liknande värderingar och mål som Sverige. Den totala föreslagna programbudgeten är cirka 80 miljoner SEK för perioden december 2024 till oktober 2028. Sveriges föreslagna bidrag till programbudgeten uppgår till 24 miljoner SEK under perioden 15 december 2024 till 30 november 2027. Sveriges stöd till budgeten för aktiviteter speglar i huvudsak den överenskomna fördelningen mellan Schweiz och Sverige (Schweiz 65 procent och Sverige 35 procent), vilket är en rimlig och logisk fördelning i förhållande till det totala bidraget från båda givarna.

The project Integrity Driven Communities contributes to the Strategy for Reform Cooperation with the Western Balkans and Turkey for 2021-2027, in the area of Human rights, Democracy, Rule of Law and Gender equality, focusing on the objective Improved conditions for accountability, increased transparency and reduced corruption. The Overall project goal is to support the creation and institutionalization of strong municipal integrity systems and practices that minimize corruption risks and increase citizens trust through: - better equipped municipalities to identify and mitigate corruption vulnerabilities, and - enhanced capacities of civil society and media to better monitor municipal decision-making processes and service delivery. As a cross cutting issue the project will support central government stakeholders to encourage the municipalities to apply good governance principles (transparency, accountability, participation, and inclusiveness) in particular related to the high corruption risk functions: public procurement and contracting, land use, licensing and permitting processes, service delivery, as well as human resources recruiting and hiring practices. Digitalization as a key component of anti-corruption efforts will be attended, especially in regards to reducing opportunities for corruption, and within the context of opening up and providing access to public interest information through online portals, databases, and websites. The municipalities will be encouraged to use Open Data and Document Management System (DMS) and to demonstrate their commitment to transparency, while using the DMS to show greater accountability. The contribution is expected to provide substantial support and focus on the power and voice of poor people and marginalized groups and to contribute to strengthening of human rights. Moreover, the project focus on municipal authorities like waste management, land use, building permits and licenses, public procurement, and public property use, make environment and climate change an important area of focus and a value that will be prioritized with this project. Gender equality will be mainstreamed in recognition of the disproportionate impact of corruption on women and girls tied to gender-based forms of corruption. Focus will be given to women belonging to ethnic minority groups, and the project will support the central government stakeholders in engaging marginalized groups , such as youth and Roma. The suggested multy-ethnic and multy -party approach with the planned project ensures a solid base for mitigating possible conflict risks. The total project budget is around 80 mSEK shared by Sweden and Switzerland for the period December 2024 - October 2028.The contribution by Sweden in the total project support is 24 mSEK for the period 15th December 2024 to 30th November 2027. The activity budget covered by Sweden mainly reflects the agreed upon allocation, between SDC and Sida at the determined rate ( SDC 65% /Sida 35%), which is a reasonable and logical approach as compared to the overall share of budget contribution by both donors.

The project Integrity Driven Communities contributes to the Strategy for Reform Cooperation with the Western Balkans and Turkey for 2021-2027, in the area of Human rights, Democracy, Rule of Law and Gender equality, focusing on the objective Improved conditions for accountability, increased transparency and reduced corruption.
Also, the institutional capacity building at national and local level and fight against corruption by strengthening the transparency and accountability of institutions is a priority according to the Sida's Revised Strategic Plan for Reform cooperation with North Macedonia 2024-2027.
This project contributes to the Agenda 2030 to SDG 5 - Achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls, sub-goal 5.5 Ensure full and effective participation and equal opportunities for leadership at all levels of decision making in political, economic and public life; SDG 16 Promote peaceful and inclusive societies for sustainable development, provide acess to justice for all and build effective,accountable and inclusive institutions at all levels, sub-goals 16.5 Substainionaly reduce Corruption and bribery in all their forms, 16.6 Develop effective, transparent and accountable institutions at all levels, 16.7 Ensure responsive, inclusive, participatory and representative decision-making at all levels, and 16.10 Ensure public acess to information and protect fundamental freedoms, in accordance to national legislation and international agreements.
Moreover, the current government of North Macedonia has clearly stated that the fight against corruption is a priority. This is confirmed through the Reform Agenda and Multiannual Work Programme submitted by North Macedonia under the Reform and Growth Facility for the Western Balkans on 23 October 2024.
Sweden provides support to combating corruption at central level with direct support to the Cabinet of the Deputy Prime Minister for Good Governance through the Support to EU integration project , as well as through provided support to investigative journalism and Support to more transparent and accountable governance. With this contribution Sweden will extend and strengthen the support at municipal level where corruption is directly affecting the citizens of the country, especially the marginalized groups, ethnic minorities, youth and women, that are disproportionately harmed by the diversion of public funds and assets for private or political gain.
Joining forces with other donors is the approach that is used to multiply the project impact in a sensitive area of reform. For this contribution Sweden will join forces with Switzerland which is a like-minded donor, that shares same values and has similar approaches in development support with Sweden.
NDI is a familiar partner to Sida that provides high quality of expertise, as well as long-term capacity built and generated project relevant knowledge from the region and globally.
The Overall project goal is to support the creation and institutionalization of strong municipal integrity systems and practices that minimize corruption risks and increase citizens trust through:
- better equipped municipalities to identify and mitigate corruption vulnerabilities, and
- enhanced capacities of civil society and media to better monitor municipal decision-making processes and service delivery.
As a cross cutting issue the project will support central government stakeholders to encourage the municipalities to apply good governance principles (transparency, accountability, participation, and inclusiveness) in particular related to the high corruption risk functions: public procurement and contracting, land use, licensing and permitting processes, service delivery, as well as human resources recruiting and hiring practices.
Digitalization as a key component of anti-corruption efforts will be attended, especially in regards to reducing opportunities for corruption, and within the context of opening up and providing access to public interest information through online portals, databases, and websites.The municipalities will be encouraged to use Open Data and Document Management System (DMS) and to demonstrate their commitment to transparency, while using the DMS to show greater accountability.
The contribution is expected to provide substantial support and focus on the power and voice of poor people and marginalized groups and to contribute to strenghtening of human rights.
Moreover, the project focus on municipal authorities like waste management, land use, building permits and licenses, public procurement, and public property use, make environment and climate change an important area of focus and a value that will be prioritized with this project.
Gender equality will be mainstreamed in recognition of the disproportionate impact of corruption on women and girls tied to gender-based forms of corruption. Focus will be given to women belonging to ethnic minority groups, and the project will support the central government stakeholders in engaging marginalized groups , such as youth and Roma.
The suggested multy-ethnic and multy -party approach with the planned project ensures a solid base for mitigating possible conflict risks.
This contribution is planned based on thorough analyses made by NDI during the inception period (December 5, 2023-October 31, 2024). In this period NDI conducted general political analyses and assessment of commitment of local authorities and involved stakeholders to the project target and planned results. The selected six pilot municipalities were supportive of the project and demonstrated initial willingness to engage.
The total project budget is around 80 mSEK shared by Sweden and Switzerland for the period December 2024 - October 2028.The contribution by Sweden in the total project support is 24 mSEK for the period 15th December 2024 to 30th November 2027. The activity budget covered by Sweden mainly reflects the agreed upon allocation, between SDC and Sida at the determined rate ( SDC 65% /Sida 35%), which is a reasonable and logical approach as compared to the overall share of budget contribution by both donors.
Based on the above assessment, Sida decides to support this project with 24 000 000 SEK for the implementing periof 15th December 2024- 30th November 2027.

The project is in its second year of implementation and operates within a politically sensitive and challenging environment. The 2025 EU progress report for North Macedonia indicates no progress in corruption prevention or prosecution of high level cases, noting that corruption remains widespread across institutions. Local governments are pointed out as part of this system, often facing challenges such as non-transparent procurement, political influence over hiring, and weak internal audit structures.
During the reporting period, effective cooperation was established with key authorities, including the Deputy Prime Minister for Good Governance, the Minister of Local Self-Government, the Minister of Justice, the State Audit Office, the State Commission for the Prevention of Corruption, and six pilot municipalities: Bitola, Bogovinje, Gazi Baba, Kumanovo, Strumica, and Shtip.
The Operational Report for the period 1 November 2024 30 June 2025 outlines the progress achieved during the initial phase of implementation.
Key results include:
- Launch of key assessments: The Assessment of Anti-Corruption Legal Frameworks, the Corruption Proofing of Legislation (CPL), and the Baseline Assessment of Public Finance Management Practices were initiated. All three assessments are currently underway and are expected to produce concrete recommendations in the next reporting period.
- Strengthening local integrity systems: The six participating municipalities made significant progress by adopting a range of internal procedures aimed at enhancing transparency, accountability, and responsible governance. Four municipalities introduced conflict-of-interest prevention procedures; four adopted internal whistle blower protection mechanisms; one regulated domestic and international business trips; one adopted rules on gifts and hospitality; and one established an internal Risk Register.
- Improved internal governance practices: Additional procedures were introduced by all six pilot municipalities to regulate participation in training and the use of representation funds, contributing to clearer internal rules and more responsible management of public resources.
- Enhanced transparency and access to information: All six municipalities developed and adopted two key internal procedures one governing free access to public information and another aimed at strengthening proactive transparency on municipal websites. These efforts align with the national Transparency Strategy (20232026) and promote more open, responsive, and citizen-oriented local governance. Publicly available procedures from Bitola, Gazi Baba, Kumanovo, and Stip can be accessed through their municipal websites.
- Stakeholder Mapping Analysis: The Integrity Driven Communities project (IDC) conducted a stakeholder mapping exercise that identified active civil society organizations in each of the six pilot municipalities. These organizations will take part in upcoming collective action initiatives supporting municipalities in strengthening their integrity systems, particularly in procurement and licensing/permitting.
- Engagement with the private sector: Cooperation was established with 19 companies from the Municipality of Shtip, resulting in findings and recommendations aimed at addressing public procurement challenges and promoting business integrity through collective action.
- Youth engagement through the Game Jam: The Empowering the Next Generation of Game Developers Game Jam engaged young creators from multiple municipalities in a month-long skills development initiative. By combining game design with civic themes, the activity demonstrated the potential of interactive media to promote democratic values. Participants developed functional game prototypes and deepened their understanding of anti-corruption, transparency, and ethical decision-making. The final showcase highlighted their ability to translate complex governance topics into meaningful game play experiences.
- Corruption Risk Assessment launched: A Corruption Risk Assessment was initiated and will provide tailored inputs for each of the six beneficiary municipalities.
Sida assesses that overall, the project is achieving satisfactory results in compliance to the approved work plan and budget and agreed project document. The project activities continue to support awareness raising and positive societal change through active engagement of municipal authorities, the private sector, and civil society organizations. The achievements to date demonstrate strong commitment among local stakeholders to improving integrity, governance practices, and public trust.
